sources.title: AC 25.1309-1A: System Design and Analysis
sources.jurisdiction: US transport-category airplane system design; historical FAA advisory material
sources.inspection_scope: Downloaded and inspected the complete 18-page advisory circular. Reviewed its stated non-mandatory status, failure-condition severity definitions, inverse probability/severity relationship, quantitative-analysis limits, and fail-safe design principles.

regions.locator: PDF pp. 1-2 and 5-7, scope, fail-safe principles and probability/severity discussion
regions.excerpt: a logical and acceptable inverse relationship between the probability and the severity of each failure condition
component failure rate data are not precise enough to enable accurate estimates

sources.limitations: This is a 1988 advisory circular, not a learned-model standard or a numerical acceptance rule for a model's perception error. It explicitly says it is guidance rather than mandatory material. Its conventional component-failure probability reasoning cannot be transferred to distribution-dependent learned behavior without a justified model of scenarios, exposure, dependencies and mitigations.

sources.title: Roadmap for Artificial Intelligence Safety Assurance, Version I
sources.inspection_scope: Copied and inspected the complete 31-page FAA roadmap from the project's retained FAA snapshot. Reviewed the safety-continuum/DAL discussion, the incremental-project approach, and the learned-implementation discussion. The source is duplicated locally for this lane but belongs to the same FAA-AI-ROADMAP evidence family as existing project records.

regions.locator: PDF pp. 11-12, incremental approach and Safety Continuum
regions.excerpt: DALs are assigned through the system safety assessment process based on the potential risks of failure or malfunction

regions.locator: PDF pp. 14-16, application to aircraft certification of learned AI implementations
regions.excerpt: existing software and complex hardware guidance is not adequate to address learned AI implementations

sources.limitations: The roadmap is a living, direction-setting document. It is not a binding means of compliance, a public approval decision, or evidence that an identified DAL has been accepted for a learned flight-critical component. Its lower-risk examples are an incremental-policy proposal, not a categorical permission boundary.

sources.title: NPA 2025-07 (B): Proposed detailed specifications and AMC & GM for AI trustworthiness (DS.AI)
sources.inspection_scope: Copied and inspected the complete 43-page EASA NPA PDF from the project's retained snapshot. Reviewed its proposed scope exclusions, AI level/authority table, operational-domain requirement and scenario hazard-likelihood risk assessment. This is the same EASA NPA evidence family as existing challenge-lane records, not independent corroboration.

regions.locator: PDF p. 4, DS.AI scope; PDF pp. 11-13, DS.AI Table 1 authority boundaries
regions.excerpt: AI-based systems presenting a risk directly contributing to the potential for fatalities

regions.locator: PDF pp. 17-20, proposed DS.AI.130 risk assessment, Tables 2–3 and qualitative-judgement limit
regions.excerpt: H1: potential for fatalities ... considered an unacceptable risk for an AI-based system operation at this point in time

regions.locator: PDF pp. 11-13, DS.AI Table 1 AI-level authority boundaries

sources.limitations: NPA 2025-07(B) is proposed material, not a final EASA decision, AMC/GM, type-certification basis or approval. The exclusions and risk table describe this proposal's scope; they do not establish a worldwide prohibition on AI functions contributing to higher-severity hazards.

sources.title: CAP3127: Detect and Avoid Policy Concept – Consultation Response Summary
sources.jurisdiction: United Kingdom uncrewed-aircraft DAA policy concept; consultation/test-phase material
sources.inspection_scope: Downloaded and inspected the complete 26-page CAP3127 PDF. Reviewed its DAA metric discussion, risk-ratio/encounter-set limits, proposed progressive test-phase approach, and statements about required evidence and future AMC/GM.

regions.locator: PDF pp. 15-16, Section 4.15 DAA metrics consultation response
regions.excerpt: RRs are essentially averaging functions and may hide deficiencies in certain encounter cases

regions.locator: PDF p. 19, Section 4.27 progressive test phase and next steps
regions.excerpt: Only after sufficient experience with this test phase, evidence of suitable performance and a lack of unexpected negative consequences

sources.limitations: This is a UK consultation response about a policy concept and its test phase, not a learned-model certification standard or proof of an approved DAA design. NMAC, DWC and risk-ratio results depend on their definitions, encounter distributions, operational restrictions and the rest of the mitigation stack.

sources.title: Assuring Machine Learning in Autonomous Systems (AMLAS), Version 1.1
sources.publisher: University of York / Assuring Autonomy International Programme
sources.jurisdiction: General learned-system assurance method; clinical example only
sources.inspection_scope: Copied and inspected the complete 60-page AMLAS v1.1 report from the project's retained snapshot. Reviewed Activity 11 and Example 32, including its ROC and confusion-matrix explanation. This is the same AMLAS evidence family as the project's assurance-challenge lane, not independent corroboration.

regions.locator: PDF pp. 34-36, Activity 11 and Example 32 / Figure 11
regions.excerpt: a trade-off is therefore required between different metrics

sources.limitations: The retinal-referral figure is an illustrative medical-classification example, not an autonomous-driving or DAA study. ROC points and confusion matrices describe performance on a defined test set and selected operating point; they do not establish operational exposure, sensor reliability, closed-loop safety, calibration under shift or certification acceptance.
